lane_title: Prompting als Bias-Mitigation in sozial sensiblen LLM-Anwendungen
scope: Primaerquellen zu 2025-2026 veroeffentlichten empirischen Untersuchungen von Prompt Engineering oder Prompting als Bias-Mitigation in LLMs, mit Schwerpunkt Gender Bias, soziale Fairness sowie Anwendungen in Gesundheit, Mental Health, Bildung, Beschaeftigung und Human Services. Preprints vor 2025 wurden nur aufgenommen, wenn 2025-2026 eine neue begutachtete Fassung erschien.

saturation.basis: Nach breiten, anwendungsbezogenen und konferenzspezifischen Suchen wurden Titel, Autor:innen, DOI- und arXiv-Identifikatoren manuell gegen die drei lokalen Quellen abgeglichen und Preprint-zu-VOR-Ketten nachverfolgt. Die letzte Folgerunde ergab ueberwiegend Dubletten, Auditstudien ohne Mitigation, technische Nicht-Promptverfahren oder schwaechere unbegutachtete Preprints.
limitations: Keine formale Datenbanksuche in Scopus oder Web of Science.
Der Royal-Society-Volltext war als CC-BY-VOR registriert, automatisierte Abrufe wurden in dieser Umgebung jedoch mit HTTP 403 abgewiesen.
Der Elsevier-Volltext zu Exploring attribution bias in LLMs war zugangsbeschraenkt; kein Preprint wurde gefunden.
Fuer die aufgenommenen reinen 2026-Preprints wurde bis zum Stichtag keine angenommene Fassung gefunden.

candidates.title: Prompting Techniques for Reducing Social Bias in LLMs through System 1 and System 2 Cognitive Processes
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 15th International Conference on Recent Advances in Natural Language Processing (RANLP 2025)
candidates.version_status: arXiv v1 2024-04-26, v4 2025-08-22; accepted main-conference proceedings version published 2025-09
candidates.peer_review_evidence: The arXiv record states Accepted at RANLP-2025 (main conference); ACL Anthology records the proceedings paper.
candidates.eligibility_technical: Compares zero-shot CoT, direct debiasing, System 1/System 2 prompts and human/machine personas across five LLMs, two datasets and nine social-bias categories; reports up to a 33 percent reduction in stereotypical judgments.
candidates.eligibility_social: Directly covers gender, race, religion, nationality, profession and other social categories and is closely aligned with socially sensitive prompt design.
notes: The local registry contains the arXiv preprint but not the RANLP 2025 proceedings version.
The most effective prompt combination varies by model and bias category.
Open preprint landing page: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.17218

candidates.title: Multi-Persona Thinking for Bias Mitigation in Large Language Models
candidates.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2026
candidates.version_status: arXiv v1 2026-01-21, v3 2026-04-21; Findings of ACL version published 2026-07
candidates.peer_review_evidence: ACL Anthology records the paper in Findings of ACL 2026.
candidates.eligibility_technical: Introduces an inference-time multi-persona framework in which contrasting social identities and a neutral perspective iteratively identify and correct biased judgments; evaluated on two established bias benchmarks with open and closed models.
candidates.eligibility_social: Explicitly models male, female and neutral viewpoints and addresses harmful social stereotypes and unfair outcomes.
notes: The authors report lower bias than existing prompting-based methods while maintaining core reasoning ability.
Open preprint landing page: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.15488

candidates.title: Prompting Fairness: Integrating Causality to Debias Large Language Models
candidates.version_status: arXiv v1 2024-03-13, v2 2025-03-02; official ICLR 2025 conference paper
candidates.peer_review_evidence: Official ICLR 2025 proceedings record and OpenReview conference-paper record.
candidates.eligibility_technical: Develops a causality-guided debiasing framework and Dual Directional Prompting; evaluates black-box LLMs on WinoBias and BBQ. On WinoBias, GPT-4 reaches a 2.17 percent pro/anti gap and 94.57 percent accuracy on anti-stereotypical cases.
candidates.eligibility_social: Targets gender and broader social bias and explicitly motivates the method with high-stakes hiring and healthcare decisions.
notes: This is distinct from the locally present work Prompting fairness: Learning prompts for debiasing large language models.
Open preprint landing page: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.08743

candidates.title: Rethinking Prompt-based Debiasing in Large Language Model
candidates.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025
candidates.version_status: arXiv preprint submitted 2025-03-12 under the plural title Large Language Models; Findings of ACL version published 2025-07 under the singular title Large Language Model
candidates.peer_review_evidence: ACL Anthology records the paper in Findings of ACL 2025.
candidates.eligibility_technical: Evaluates prompt-based debiasing on BBQ and StereoSet with open models and GPT; shows that lower bias scores can result from evasive Unknown responses and reduced task accuracy. Llama2-7B-Chat misclassified more than 90 percent of unbiased content as biased.
candidates.eligibility_social: Provides a necessary validity check for claimed social-bias mitigation and for evaluations used to justify deployment in socially sensitive contexts.
notes: The paper argues that fairness, task accuracy and answer evasion must be evaluated together.
Open preprint landing page: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.09219

candidates.title: Toward True Neutrality: Evaluating Inference-Time Debiasing Strategies for Gender Coreference Resolution in LLMs
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 39th Pacific Asia Conference on Language, Information and Computation
candidates.version_status: official PACLIC 2025 proceedings version; no preprint found
candidates.peer_review_evidence: ACL Anthology records the paper in the PACLIC 2025 proceedings.
candidates.eligibility_technical: Compares self-correction, self-consistency and chain-of-thought for occupational gender coreference while measuring bias reduction and computational cost; low-bias-feedback self-correction improves performance by up to 41 percent over self-consistent prompting.
candidates.eligibility_social: Directly addresses gender bias affecting women and non-binary people in a task motivated by healthcare, education and finance deployments.
notes: The study also qualitatively analyzes bias, logic and grammaticality patterns in chain-of-thought responses.
No DOI is listed in ACL Anthology.

candidates.title: Mitigating medical bias in large language models by prompt engineering: an empirical study of effectiveness and trade-offs
candidates.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A, 384(2324), article 20250125
candidates.version_status: version of record; no preprint found
candidates.peer_review_evidence: Published as a journal article by the Royal Society in Philosophical Transactions A.
candidates.eligibility_technical: Evaluates five prompting strategies across five LLMs on a medical-bias benchmark, jointly measuring fairness, accuracy and inference overhead. Chain-of-thought reduces the average group gap by 2.4 percentage points, with a maximum reduction of 6.2 points and significant reductions in 8 of 15 McNemar comparisons.
candidates.eligibility_social: Directly addresses fair healthcare and patient-safety risks for groups defined by sensitive attributes.
notes: No prompting strategy is universally effective, and some exacerbate bias.
The VOR is registered under CC BY 4.0, but automated publisher retrieval returned HTTP 403 in this environment.
Authoritative abstract and metadata: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42463224/

candidates.title: Patient Cognitive Bias in Large Language Model-Supported Health Consultations: Simulation-Based Comparative Study
candidates.venue: Journal of Medical Internet Research, 28, e85770
candidates.version_status: JMIR preprint submitted 2025-10-13, accepted 2026-05-04; journal version published 2026-06-11
candidates.peer_review_evidence: JMIR records the original paper and an explicit submitted/accepted open-review history.
candidates.eligibility_technical: Uses 1273 MedQA-USMLE cases, six LLMs, three-round consultations, three prompt mitigations and four temperature settings. Patient bias reduces accuracy by about 7-39 percentage points; prompting is limited and inconsistent, while a separate reasoning system gains about 10-39 points.
candidates.eligibility_social: Directly evaluates patient-facing health consultations and user-driven cognitive bias in an interactive Human Services setting.
notes: The all-inclusive prompt provides the most consistent but generally modest prompt-level gains.
Open review/version landing page: https://preprints.jmir.org/preprint/85770/accepted

candidates.title: Gender Bias in LLM Hiring Decisions: Evidence from a Japanese Context and Evaluation of Mitigation Strategies
candidates.version_status: arXiv v1; no accepted conference or journal version found by the cutoff date
candidates.peer_review_evidence: No peer-review evidence found; preprint only.
candidates.eligibility_technical: Counterfactual design with 60 Japanese rirekisho resumes, 12 gender-signaling name pairs, five LLMs and 43200 API calls across baseline, gender-neutrality instruction and privacy-filter conditions. The prompt instruction does not meaningfully reduce bias; removing names removes nearly the full effect.
candidates.eligibility_social: Direct gender-bias evidence in hiring, with a non-Western setting and practical privacy/refusal trade-offs relevant to personnel and case decisions.
notes: The privacy-filter condition produces a 42 percent refusal rate for GPT-4o.
Findings remain provisional because the work is not peer reviewed.

candidates.title: BiasFreeBench: a Benchmark for Mitigating Bias in Large Language Model Responses
candidates.version_status: arXiv v1 2025-09-30, v2 2026-02-15; accepted ICLR 2026 paper
candidates.peer_review_evidence: Official ICLR 2026 proceedings record; arXiv states Accepted by ICLR 2026.
candidates.eligibility_technical: Benchmarks four prompt-based and four training-based methods across seven LLMs, BBQ and FairMT-Bench; prompt methods are generally stronger, with chain-of-thought often best and self-awareness relatively efficient.
candidates.eligibility_social: Covers nine social-bias types, including gender, age, disability and socioeconomic status.
notes: Tier B because it is a general benchmark without a concrete Human Services application setting.

candidates.title: No Free Lunch in Language Model Bias Mitigation? Targeted Bias Reduction Can Exacerbate Unmitigated LLM Biases
candidates.version_status: arXiv preprint submitted 2025-11-23; journal version published 2026
candidates.peer_review_evidence: MDPI journal version and public review-report page.
candidates.eligibility_technical: Runs 160 debiasing experiments and 640 evaluations across ten models, four techniques and four StereoSet dimensions. Significant on-target improvement occurs in 20.6 percent of cases; significant spillover harm occurs in 31.5 percent.
candidates.eligibility_social: Directly examines cross-effects among gender, race, religion and profession bias.
notes: Tier B because prompt debiasing is only one of four interventions and the application remains a generic StereoSet evaluation.

candidates.title: Can Fairness Be Prompted? Prompt-Based Debiasing Strategies in High-Stakes Recommendations
candidates.version_status: arXiv v1; no accepted venue found by the cutoff date
candidates.peer_review_evidence: No peer-review evidence found; preprint only.
candidates.eligibility_technical: Tests three bias-aware prompt strategies with three LLMs, four templates, nine sensitive-attribute values and two recommendation datasets; reports fairness improvements up to 74 percent with possible overpromotion.
candidates.eligibility_social: Applies prompting to employment and news recommendations where inferred gender and age can affect outcomes.
notes: Tier B because the evidence is an unreviewed single-version preprint.

candidates.title: Hedging and Non-Affirmation: Quantifying LLM Alignment on Questions of Human Rights
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency
candidates.version_status: arXiv v1 2025-02-26, v2 2026-04-06; FAccT 2026 version published 2026-06-25
candidates.eligibility_technical: Evaluates seven LLMs on 4738 prompts across 205 national and stateless identities; group steering is the most effective mitigation and is robust to downstream forgetting.
candidates.eligibility_social: Directly measures identity-dependent hedging and non-affirmation in human-rights statements.
notes: Tier B because the mitigation uses activation steering and orthogonalization rather than prompt engineering.
The ACM VOR is marked CC BY 4.0.

candidates.title: Mental Health Equity in LLMs: Leveraging Multi-Hop Question Answering to Detect Amplified and Silenced Perspectives
candidates.version_status: arXiv v1; marked Under Review; no accepted version found by the cutoff date
candidates.peer_review_evidence: No completed peer review; the arXiv record says Under Review.
candidates.eligibility_technical: Uses IMHI material, multi-hop question answering, four LLMs and intersectional tags; roleplay simulation and explicit bias-reduction few-shot prompts report 66-94 percent bias reductions.
candidates.eligibility_social: Directly covers mental-health discourse at intersections of age, race, gender and socioeconomic status.
notes: Tier B because the large reported effects lack completed peer review and independent validation.

candidates.title: 'Rich Dad, Poor Lad': How do Large Language Models Contextualize Socioeconomic Factors in College Admission?
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
candidates.version_status: arXiv preprint submitted 2025-09-19; EMNLP 2025 main-conference version published 2025-11
candidates.peer_review_evidence: ACL Anthology records an EMNLP 2025 main-conference paper.
candidates.eligibility_technical: Audits four open LLMs with 30000 synthetic applicant profiles and five million prompts under decision-only and explanation-based modes; explanation prompting amplifies socioeconomic-status compensation reasoning.
candidates.eligibility_social: Directly addresses socioeconomic fairness in college admissions and is strongly relevant to education.
notes: Tier B because prompt mode is an audit condition rather than a tested mitigation intervention.

candidates.title: How LLM Counselors Violate Ethical Standards in Mental Health Practice: A Practitioner-Informed Framework
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society, 8(2)
candidates.peer_review_evidence: Official AIES proceedings record, Main Track II.
candidates.eligibility_technical: Combines an 18-month ethnographic collaboration with three psychologists and seven peer counselors with expert evaluation of 137 sessions, yielding 15 ethical violations in five themes.
candidates.eligibility_social: Directly examines mental-health counseling, discrimination, cultural insensitivity, user agency, crisis management and unequal effects of digital literacy.
notes: Tier B because it is an ethics audit and does not experimentally evaluate a bias-mitigation prompt.

candidates.title: Evaluating anti-LGBTQIA+ medical bias in large language models
candidates.version_status: medRxiv preprint chain followed by peer-reviewed PLOS Digital Health version
candidates.peer_review_evidence: PLOS identifies the work as a peer-reviewed research article and exposes its peer-review record.
candidates.eligibility_technical: Tests four LLMs with 38 clinician- and LGBTQIA+-expert-designed prompt pairs and medical review of safety, privacy, accuracy and bias.
candidates.eligibility_social: Directly addresses health inequity and differential harms for LGBTQIA+ patients.
notes: Tier B because it is an audit/benchmark without an evaluated mitigation intervention.
PLOS states CC BY open access.

candidates.title: New model, old risks: sociodemographic bias and adversarial hallucinations vulnerability in GPT-5
candidates.version_status: medRxiv preprint published 2025-09-21; npj Digital Medicine version published 2026-04-04
candidates.peer_review_evidence: Published in npj Digital Medicine; PubMed links the preprint as updated by the journal article.
candidates.eligibility_technical: Re-evaluates GPT-5 on 500 emergency vignettes across 32 sociodemographic labels and adversarial prompts. An explicit mitigation prompt reduces adversarial hallucination from 65 percent to 7.67 percent.
candidates.eligibility_social: Shows persistent demographic variation and 100 percent mental-health-screening recommendations for several LGBTQIA+ groups in controlled clinical cases.
notes: Tier B because the mitigation prompt targets adversarial hallucination rather than the measured sociodemographic bias.

candidates.title: Exploring attribution bias in LLMs: Social influences and prompt-based mitigation
candidates.version_status: publisher version of record; no preprint found
candidates.peer_review_evidence: Published as a journal article in Technology in Society.
candidates.eligibility_technical: Controlled experiment with five LLMs manipulating event valence, attribution perspective, gender, age, education and region; prompt interventions reduce attributional extremity.
candidates.eligibility_social: Connects social cognition and fairness to high-stakes settings including education, law and healthcare.
notes: Tier B because the setting is general attribution rather than a direct Human Services task.
Publisher full text is restricted; only the publisher abstract was verifiable.
